channel.title: Hack the Platform Blog
channel.description: Insights, tutorials, and stories about Microsoft Power Platform and beyond. Empower your business with Power Apps, Power Automate, Copilot Agents, and more.

item.title: Block Copilot Studio in Default Environment with a Simple Plugin
item.description: Learn how to prevent users from creating Copilot agents in the Default Power Platform environment using a simple Dataverse plugin.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Converting CSV to JSON in Power Platform
item.description: Unlock the potential of your data with our comprehensive guide on converting CSV files to JSON format using Power Platform. Learn step-by-step processes, tips, and tricks to seamlessly transform your data for enhanced analysis and integration. Dive into the power of Power Platform and elevate your data handling skills today!
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Dataflows Part 1 - Choice Column with Single Value
item.description: Learn how to work with single-value Choice columns in Dataverse and configure them with Dataflows.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Dataflows Part 4 - LookUp Column with Multiple Values (Many-to-Many Relationships)
item.description: How to handle many-to-many relationships in Dataverse using Dataflows, with a detailed comparison of manual vs built-in approaches.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Dataflows Part 3 - LookUp Column with Single Value
item.description: In Part 3 of the Dataflows series, we focus on working with Dataverse Lookup Columns (Single Values) and how to prepare, map, and validate them in Power Platform dataflows.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Dataflows Part 2 - Choice Column with Multiple Values
item.description: Learn how to handle multi-select Choice columns from SharePoint and map them into Dataverse using Power Query dataflows. This post walks through creating a custom lookup table, expanding and merging multiple values, and grouping them back into a format that Dataverse can store. Includes step-by-step guidance and Power Query code snippets.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: How to Delete AgentBuilder Agents Automatically
item.description: Automatically detect and delete Copilot Studio AgentBuilder agents using Power Automate and the Power Platform Inventory API.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Custom Connector for Power Automate Approvals
item.description: Learn how to build a reusable Custom Connector for Power Automate Approvals and integrate it into Power Apps.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Auto-Generate Azure Blob Folders from Dataverse Using a Plugin
item.description: Learn how to create a Dataverse plugin that automatically creates Azure Blob Storage folders for new records using REST API calls.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Power Pages & SPA (Part 1): Deploying a Custom React SPA to Microsoft Power Pages
item.description: Learn how to build a Vite + React Single Page Application, deploy it to Power Pages using the official Power Platform CLI, and preserve your configuration safely.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Liquid vs Web API in Power Pages: Data Loading Performance
item.description: In this post, I compare the performance of Liquid and Web API in Power Pages when rendering large datasets. Based on real-world tests with 200, 2,000, and 10,000 records, I analyze which approach delivers faster page loads, better scalability, and a smoother user experience. You’ll also learn best practices for data filtering, server-side calls, and asynchronous loading to avoid common performance pitfalls.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Power Pages & SPA (Part 2): Adding Authentication with Microsoft Entra ID
item.description: In this second part of the Power Pages & SPA series, we add authentication to our custom React single-page application using Microsoft Entra ID and Power Pages user context.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Power Pages & SPA (Part 3): Fetching Dataverse Data Securely
item.description: In Part 3, we’ll connect our Power Pages + React SPA to Dataverse using the Web API. You’ll learn to enable API access, set permissions for authenticated users, and securely fetch data with CSRF token handling. We’ll also build a simple UI to display Accounts, validating our authentication setup from Part 2.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Power Pages & SPA (Part 4): Starting a Power Automate Flow from React SPA
item.description: Learn how to securely start a Power Automate flow from your React SPA in Power Pages, fetching Dataverse data without exposing tables or permissions.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: Power Pages & SPA Part 5: Using Server Logic in React SPA
item.description: How to call Power Pages Server Logic from a React SPA using Microsoft Entra ID app credentials stored in Power Pages site settings and environment variables.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)

item.title: How to delete connections from the environment
item.description: Cleaning up **shared_logicflows** connections in error state is essential for maintaining a healthy Power Platform environment. By following the steps outlined in this blog post, you’ll keep your connections tidy and improve overall performance.
item.author: fukszon.kostya@gmail.com (Konstantin Fukszon)
